tagline: World-class mountain resorts and premium lodging experiences
hero_kpi_rationale: Revenue from pass products is the primary driver of predictability and customer loyalty, representing 65% of lift revenue, making it a key performance indicator and a sustainable competitive advantage.

kpis.name: Pass products share of lift revenue
kpis.explanation: Proportion of lift revenue derived from season passes (such as the Epic Pass) sold prior to the ski season.
kpis.description: Passes like the Epic Pass are sold in advance, providing strong revenue visibility. A high share indicates strong customer loyalty and improved financial predictability.
kpis.signal: 65% of lift revenue comes from passes and three-year averages show growth from 61% to 65%

kpis.name: Mountain segment share of total revenue
kpis.explanation: The Mountain segment represents the vast majority of the company's revenue.
kpis.description: The Mountain segment is the company's core, generating 89% of revenue from ski operations and lift services.
kpis.signal: The core business is clearly skiing and lift operations with 89% of revenue

kpis.name: Long-haul visitor share
kpis.explanation: Proportion of skiers traveling from distant locations (out-of-state or international) at key resorts.
kpis.description: Long-haul guests spend more and utilize more ancillary services. A decline may signal economic or geopolitical pressures.
kpis.signal: Slight decline in long-haul visitors from 57% to 56% indicates potential pressure on premium demand

kpis.name: Lift revenue share of Mountain revenue
kpis.explanation: Lift ticket sales represent approximately 57% of Mountain segment revenue.
kpis.description: Despite ancillary services, lift operations remain the primary revenue source within the Mountain segment.
kpis.signal: Core Mountain revenue remains lift tickets at 57%, stable over three years

kpis.name: Lodging segment share of total revenue
kpis.explanation: The Lodging segment contributes approximately 11% of total revenue.
kpis.description: Lodging (hotels, condos, NPS) is closely tied to Mountain segment performance.
kpis.signal: Secondary but complementary segment to skiing, stable at 11% of total revenue

kpis.name: Real Estate segment share of total revenue
kpis.explanation: The Real Estate segment contributes marginally to total revenue.
kpis.description: The Real Estate segment did not contribute to net revenue in 2025, likely due to absence of significant real estate sales.
kpis.signal: Real estate revenue negligible in 2025, 0% of total revenue

kpis.name: Pass revenue share of lift revenue
kpis.explanation: Key indicator of customer loyalty and revenue predictability.
kpis.description: Since 2023, this share has increased from 61% to 65%, reflecting the accelerating success of the Epic Pass program and strengthened customer loyalty.
kpis.signal: Sustained growth since 2023 (61% to 65%) reflects the success of the Epic Pass program

kpis.name: Long-haul visitor share
kpis.explanation: Measures resort appeal to national and international visitors.
kpis.description: In 2025, the share of long-haul visitors declined by one point, from 57% to 56%, suggesting increased sensitivity to economic or geopolitical conditions.
kpis.signal: Slight decline of one point after two stable years at 57% signals moderate pressure on premium demand

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 declared fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Total revenue of 2.964 Bn USD last fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 declared fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of 0.28 Bn USD last fiscal year (FY2025).

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or related technologies in the provided documents. The company does not position AI as a strategic lever.
evidence: No reference to AI, machine learning, or advanced automation in the 10-K
No mention of digital tools or predictive analytics in pass or demand management
Focus on physical experience, subscription-based loyalty, and seasonal operations
